newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Police, leftist supporters scuffle in Jakarta.
newsitem.headline: Police, leftist supporters scuffle in Jakarta.

text.p: More than 100 supporters of Indonesian leftists on trial in Jakarta on subversion charges scuffled with police outside a court on Monday, but later dispersed, witnesses said.
The disturbance began after three members of the left-wing People's Democratic Party (PRD) walked out of a hearing and went to their holding room in the Jakarta Central State Court.
The Marxist-leaning PRD is banned from Indonesia's general election to be held on May 29, for which campaigning began on Sunday.
Only three political parties are permitted to contest the elections, the ruling Golkar, and the minority United Development Party and Indonesian Democratic Party.
Supporters of the three defendants in the central Jakarta court left the building and gathered on a street outside.
The prosecution has called for varying prison terms for 10 PRD members accused of subversion following riots which rocked Jakarta in July last year.
Witnesses said police beat and detained three PRD supporters outside the court.
No trouble was reported from the South Jakarta State Court where verdicts were being read out to the other seven PRD defendants.
